messages:
support-sam: :rotating_light: Support escalation - multiple customers hitting 5xx / timeouts on Hosted Inference API since ~2026-03-15 09:18 PST. Getting a lot of 502/504 and upstream read timeouts. Sample response from customer:
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\ncontent-type: application/json\n{"error":"gateway_timeout", "message": "upstream read timeout", "request_id": "abc123-req"}

support-sam: Repro steps we used locally (customer-supplied):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "X-Request-ID: abc123-req" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-base","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
They see ~30-60% error rate. Ticket #CUST-4321 attached. Escalating to SRE / oncall. cc @ops-oncall @maria-l @raj

incident-bot: Incident created: hosted-inference-5xx-1845012345 (priority: P1). War room: https://zoom.example/room-1845012345

ops-oncall: I'm on it. Pulling logs + tracing now. First glance: gateway pods show repeated `upstream read timeout` and 502s. Runtime (inference) pods are healthy but CPU pinned on a few nodes. Spikes from us-west-2 region around 09:16-09:22 PST. Giving timeline in a sec.

maria-l: Graphs: https://grafana.example/d/hosted/gateway-5xx?orgId=1&from=1645011000000
There is a sharp increase in gateway 5xx starting 09:17. Correlates with a change in HAProxy/edge timeouts deployed 09:15 in commit 9a8b7c. That change lowered proxy read timeout to 2s (was 10s) — looks too aggressive for some models with cold starts.

raj: Confirmed. Looking at kube events and autoscaler logs — horizontal-pod-autoscaler didn't scale quick enough; cooldown/thresholds prevented scale out for a burst. Also seeing long model shard load times causing backend delays. Trying a soft rollback of the proxy config and nudging HPA.

eng-alex: Can we divert heavy enterprise customers to Dedicated pool temporarily? That would reduce pressure on hosted runtime. If feasible we can add routing rule by customer tag.

ops-oncall: Yes — implementing traffic-split: route `customer_tag:enterprise-123` to `dedicated-backup` pool. Applying via control-plane API now:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood.internal/v1/routing/split \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"match":{"customer_tag":"enterprise-123"},"route":"dedicated-backup"}'
```

sre-bot: deploybot: Starting rollback of edge-proxy config to commit 6f4d2a to restore previous timeouts.

maria-l: Rolling back HAProxy change now. Patch:
```
kubectl -n infra set image deployment/edge-proxy edge-proxy=registry.redwood/edge-proxy:6f4d2a
kubectl rollout status deploy/edge-proxy -n infra
```

sre-bot: deploybot: rollout started for edge-proxy (namespace=infra) — 3/3 updated.

ops-oncall: Also increasing HPA maxReplicas for hosted-runtime to 50 from 20 to allow faster scaling, and lowering scale target CPU from 70% -> 55% temporarily.

maria-l: Patch applied and timeouts reverted. Early signal: 5xx rate dropping for effected customers, from 45% -> 10% in the last 5m. Keep monitoring.

support-sam: Notifying affected customers: sent initial update and ETA 30m for full mitigation. Asking them to share any logs/trace ids. Ticket #CUST-4321 updated.

raj: Restarted a couple of gateway pods to clear stuck connections: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/hosted-gateway -n prod`. Watch for crashloops.

sre-bot: k8s-bot: hosted-gateway rollout completed (6/6 pods). No CrashLoopBackOff observed.

eng-alex: Thanks — can we enable a temporary autoscaling policy override for the next 2 hours to handle any bursts? If so, we should document the change and revert later.

ops-oncall: Done — policy override applied via ops console. Also added a temporary fallback routing rule to route to smaller-but-stable quantized model variant for latency-sensitive endpoints to reduce backend load.

maria-l: Found one more thing: an older ingress rule was inadvertently sending a small percentage of traffic to a legacy runtime with higher cold-starts. Flipping that off.

rachel: Good work team. Once the immediate pressure is down, we need a short postmortem and follow-ups. Please capture actions and owners here. I'll draft the postmortem template after final status.

support-sam: Customers replying: most say errors subsided; one enterprise reports occasional 502s but much improved. Marking customer comms as 'follow-up required'.

ops-oncall: Current status: mitigations applied, 5xx rate reduced to <5% overall, targeted customers in green except one long-tail. I'm going to keep war room open for 30m then hand off to oncall for monitoring.

maria-l: Root cause hypothesis summary: aggressive proxy timeout change (commit 9a8b7c) + HPA threshold/cooldown + a small fraction of traffic routed to legacy runtime => amplified cold-starts and backend timeouts.

rachel: Postmortem action items (assignments + tentative due dates):
- ACTION-1: Revert and add safety check for proxy timeout changes (owner: maria-l, due: 2026-03-18). Ticket: INF-8821
- ACTION-2: Tweak HPA autoscaling policies/give more aggressive burst scaling for inference pools (owner: raj, due: 2026-03-20). Ticket: INF-8822
- ACTION-3: Add gating in deploy pipeline to block proxy timeout < 5s without perf tests (owner: eng-alex, due: 2026-03-22). Ticket: INF-8823
- ACTION-4: Route fallback / model-variant policy documentation and runbook (owner: ops-oncall, due: 2026-03-19). Ticket: INF-8824
- ACTION-5: Customer comms postmortem note + SRE runbook for enterprise SLA calls (owner: support-sam, due: 2026-03-18). Ticket: INF-8825

rachel: Also want a follow-up: add synthetic tests for cold-start tail latencies (owner: maria-l, due: 2026-03-25). Ticket: INF-8826

ops-oncall: Filing a rolling postmortem now and will attach logs/traces. I'll handoff to rachel and support-sam for final external comms. Leaving monitoring on for 2h.

support-sam: Thanks all. I'll keep ticket updates and send the draft customer-facing note once we have the postmortem bullet list.

rachel: Closing war room in 30m unless more regressions. Good job responding quickly. :thumbsup:

support-sam: closing note — incident mitigated. Will follow up with postmortem and action items. :white_check_mark:
